annotation.title_clean: Уголовно-правовое регулирование робототехники: результаты социологического исследования
annotation.title_en: Criminal Law Regulation of Robotics: Results of a Sociological Study
named_instruments_referenced: Criminal Code of the Russian Federation
annotation.summary_en: Russian journal article reporting a survey on the criminal law regulation of robotics. It looks at how to define "robot", criminal liability for crimes committed with robots, and robots as targets of crimes. Respondents support binding rules on creating and using robots, and on making the creation of robots for criminal purposes a separate crime.
key_provisions_or_claims: 92.8% of respondents believe robots can be used to commit crimes
52.7% think creating a robot for criminal purposes should itself be a crime; 44.6% treat it as preparation for a crime
Most respondents support legally binding rules on creating, operating, repairing and using robots
The author argues that creating a criminal robot should become a separate offence in Russian criminal law
Respondents link the risks posed by robots to the need for comprehensive regulation
